text_fidelity_a:
Thames & Kosmos Crystal Growing Science Kit Grow Over A Dozen Crystals with 15 Experiments, Includes Storage Case & 32 Page Color Laboratory Manual My child's science project last year was growing crystals. We had lots of fun using different temperature liquids, chemicals, etc. to see which would grow fastest, best, make the most solid of crystals and even made rock candy as a "take home" treat. I love the creativity of this kit. It allows for you to create UP TO 13 different experiments (but if you cheat you can get a couple more out of it). Some of the chemicals used are not safe for young kids so I'd highly suggest sticking to the recommended manufacturer's age. Not to mention the fact that some of the crystals will take longer than a week to fully form -- most kids don't have the patience to wait. Not waiting the proper amount of time to ensure the solidity of the crystals will result in disappointment as you can imagine something that isn't solid enough can break very easy. Following directions is paramount! Make sure you sit with your child and read through all of the instructions before beginning. I'd suggest sticking with the easiest project first to get their feet wet on experimenting then gradually go through the "harder" ones. I do like that the simple purchase of extra chemicals (or using sugar) can add a lot more fun to your kit. Thames & Kosmos is a good company. They even provide online printable instructions along side the greatly illustrated manual. http://www.thamesandkosmos.com/news/manualsamples/659127_glowingcrystals_manual_sample.pdf
The price of the kit is very fair. In fact, I'd say it would be an excellent science fair project to conduct with your child this spring. Start practicing now and wow the judges with modified versions. Just be sure to do your homework. Check out books from your local library on growing crystals and start taking notes. This could be a really fun learning experience for grade-schoolers and homeschoolers alike. The only thing I thought was slightly cheesy was the "treasure case" and the shapes (thus my four stars). But kids will get a kick out of them.
text_fidelity_b: Thames & Kosmos Crystal Growing Science Kit Grow Over A Dozen Crystals with 15 Experiments, Includes Storage Case & 32 Page Color Laboratory Manual

PLANET BAKE Donut Baking Kit - Vegan Chocolate Donuts with Pre-Measured Ingredients and No Added Sugar- Complete Chef Kit Idea for Boys and Girls ages 4-12 I'm not at all pleased with this donut kit. I like the idea -- a kit that includes everything needed to make baked, frosted donuts that kids (with supervision) can take on as a fun project. Unfortunately, the execution of the idea was not done well.

The items come in a flimsy cardboard box that is easily dented up in transit. It makes for a poor presentation should this be a gift item sent to child. Inside the box is a set of cheap silicone molds for the donuts, a packet of sprinkles and a sealed packet with the mixes. The sprinkle packet opened up in transit so there were sprinkles everywhere. Inside the sealed packet the frosting mix is in a pouch, but the donut mix is just loose in the pouch. Getting the frosting packet out was a very messy proposition.

Making the mix is simple (needs water and oil). The included silicone molds are very thin and flimsy, and need to be inserted into a muffin pan to minimize the chance of spilling. This is the step kids will need the most assistance with.

But even if the donuts bake properly, they are no treat to eat. The chocolate flavor is not pleasant, and is made even worse by the artificial sweetener aftertaste. The texture is not bad considering these are gluten-free, but the taste is not good to the point where these are barely (and I mean barely!) edible.

Two stars for the overall concept of a donut kit as a fun kid project (both making and decorating) but everything else is a fail.
text_fidelity_b: PLANET BAKE Donut Baking Kit - Vegan Chocolate Donuts with Pre-Measured Ingredients and No Added Sugar- Complete Chef Kit Idea for Boys and Girls ages 4-12

Fisher-Price Octonauts Sea-Slimed Octopod Playset My boys are currently loving all things Octonauts. Before Christmas arrived, my 3 year old was pretending that Legos were each of the Octonauts. While there's nothing wrong with using his imagination, it was becoming very difficult for us to keep up with exactly which Lego was which Octonaut. He was frustrated at our lack of help when it came to locating a specific piece.

This Octopod has been well loved! As far as characters go, this set only comes with Captain Barnacles. We bought other characters separately to make playing with it more fun, though. It also comes with a container of "sea slime". I dislike this stuff greatly, but my children enjoyed it while it lasted. It didn't make a huge mess, and it's not overly sticky, but touching a piece here and there that escaped from the rest was gross. (Reaching under a bed and feeling cold slime isn't the greatest feeling.) The set even comes with a catapult to throw the sea slime, but I really don't recommend doing that.

Assembly is pretty easy. Several pieces have to snap together, and there's several stickers to put into place, but it happens quickly. Be careful with the stickers. Once you stick them, they're stuck. I have a couple of them the slightest bit crooked, but I couldn't fix it. It uses batteries, but those are already included. There's a button to press to hear sound effects(from the show). I didn't find this horribly annoying, but I do actually like the show.

My only complaint is that the top of the Octopod is hard to close properly. My youngest was very frustrated with it at first, and asked for help with it. It seems he's accepted that it won't close just right at this point, and mostly plays with it with the top open.

Overall, my boys have had great fun playing with it. It's been a great addition to the Gups they also got for Christmas.
text_fidelity_b: Fisher-Price Octonauts Sea-Slimed Octopod Playset

text_fidelity_a:
Bezier Games Palace of Mad King Ludwig Palaces of Mad King Ludwig is a tile-laying, castle-building game for two to four players. This game is reminiscent of Carcassonne, except it is a good bit more complicated, requiring players to place building tiles near each other in specific patterns to earn swans of various colors, utilize special powers or scoring rules, and to build both above and below ground while the moat around the castle continually encloses your playspace.

Ultimately, while the components are nice quality, there are quite a lot of bits for a game like this, and the artwork is not particularly interesting. Rooms are largely void of identifiable decoration, making the words easy to read, but the rooms difficult to distinguish. Also of note, in the previous "Mad King" game, a major selling point of the game was mismatched and oddly sized tiles, while this one is entirely composed of squares and rectangles.

All told, we fell like this was a solid game, but one that has just a few too many rules that confine what you can do and what you want to do. Most of the time, there was a clear "best move" available, and rarely were more than, say, three decisions even possible based on what you could buy and where you could place it. I think a lot of people will like this game more than I did, as my fellow players certainly did. I would personally rather play something that is more streamlined (Carcassonne), or simply more interesting (Castles of Mad King Ludwig).

Also of note, Palace of Mad King Ludwig is not related to it's cousin "Castles," which is a little confusing. The idea behind the games is radically different.
text_fidelity_b: Bezier Games Palace of Mad King Ludwig

text_fidelity_a:
Matchbox Aqua Cannon Fire Truck Rig [[VIDEOID:f267642283bcf2ef6b127013dc46be9b]] On the advertising, this says that it shoots 20 feet. I was really skeptical, and I was expecting it to only shoot 20 feet in the air. Now, I don't have a 20 foot ladder, so I can't tell for sure, but I'm pretty sure that this will shoot vertically 20 feet, and horizontally maybe even a little more.

The truck is big and bulky, which I really liked. And there are no small, removable parts, so it's probably good for kids of any age. It does shoot a pretty powerful stream of water, so the only danger is squirting friends, family, and pets in the eye.

Now, about the water, the truck doesn't hold very much water. It says that it will shoot 50 shots of water, and it does do that. This is a lot like one of those water conserving showers. It really doesn't use very much water, but you can't really tell that until you fill it up. So, it's not the best thing for a water fight. But it is a great gift for youngsters so they don't get their siblings too wet. And I did really like the bright, vivid colors.

The wheels rotate, but they can't turn. If you need to turn this, you'll need to pick it up and move it around. Really, the only movable part on this is the fire hose.

Pros:
+Big and bulky
+Fun for all ages
+Shoots water a long way
+You can position the fire hose a little

Cons:
-A little hard to aim
-Wheels can't turn right or left, only rotate straight ahead
-Doesn't hold a ton of water
-You can't build up pressure to do a power squirt
text_fidelity_b: Matchbox Aqua Cannon Fire Truck Rig

text_fidelity_a:
Aerobie Pro Ring Outdoor Kids Toy for Boys and Girls, All Ages, Colors may Vary This is a great ring! Once you get your hands on the comfortable, flexible silicone body, you'll want to throw it. Children of all ages and even grown men cannot resist chucking it as far as they can. These big rings sail FAAAAR! And they are a tad prone to getting stuck in high and sometimes funny places. (Believe me, these will end up in the trees and on roofs but they are easy to get down with a broom stick because of their ring shape.)

A boy at cub scouts had one of these that everyone was playing with last week. My son decided to spend his hard earned allowance money on Amazon to order one, hoping it wouldn't be pink. :) He was thrilled when a yellow ring arrived. It has a VERY rice, silicone-like, soft rubbery grip and is fun to throw! Kids fight over these rings so I'm thinking of ordering several for birthday gifts and cousin Christmas gifts. You can't beat a gift for under ten that kids actually want to play outside with!

Consider spending a little more and buying the 13 inch ring. It flies farther and better than the 10 inch rings did. However, if you don't have a wide open play space, the 10 inch rings might be better because they play more like a Frisbee and don't get hung up in trees quite as easily.

UPDATE: I am now buying our THIRD ring! These make awesome gifts for boys in the 8 to 11 range, as my son is frequently swarmed by boys wanting to play with his. But be aware that if you throw it too far and loose sight of it, you won't get it back. It will be stolen by the first kid who comes across it. We had this happen at a party where the ring ended up sailing over a house and landing far behind it in an empty field right at dark. It was snatched before daylight. Hence me having to buy our third. (Since it was probably the roving neighborhood teenagers who picked it up late that night, I am going to say this is a good toy for fussy 16 and 17 year-olds, too!) It has been a favorite gift at birthday parties, followed by thank yous from the moms who are grateful for any toy that gets their video game addicted boys outside. I am thrilled to have found such a good gift for under $10. You can't go wrong with this ring!

Update March 2017: I have now ordered nearly 10 of these rings in the last 5 months for birthday gifts for 9 and 10 year old boys and without fail, it has been an instant hit. The boys are always eager to show how FAR they can throw the ring and then are shocked when it sails two hundred yards or more. They puff out their chests as their friends exclaim "WOOOAH!" while the ring whizzes one or two streets over and then the birthday boy swaggers off to fetch the ring with every other boy tagging along, begging for a turn to throw it next. Children now double check with my son to ensure that he's going to get them an Aerobie ring for their birthday. I keep at least one on-hand for last minute birthday party invites.

• COLORS •

Out of all the rings we have ordered, only 1 has been pink. We have received 2 orange, 1 pink and all the rest have been yellow. Trying to get a big pink ring for a girl's birthday party coming up in May is proving challenging since we keep getting shipped yellow!
text_fidelity_b: Aerobie Pro Ring Outdoor Kids Toy for Boys and Girls, All Ages, Colors may Vary

text_fidelity_a:
Ludonaute Fantasy Flight Games LUCV01 Carta Imperia Victoria, Multicolor CIV is a very good small card game. It takes about a half hour to play, and is largely comprised of cards with silly cartoonish art on them representing science, military, culture and so forth. Basically, if it's in Sid Meier's Civilization, it has been boiled down and reduced to a small concept here.

The artwork is...interesting. Some people will love it's uniqueness, while others will find it to be off-putting. I tend to fall in the latter column - it doesn't look like it matches with the theme of the game at all. The player aids are good, but small (probably to fit in the box), and can be difficult to read. It would have been better, in my opinion, to put some more text on each individual card instead of trying to stuff all the text onto one very small aid.

These are quibbles. The game is fast, interesting, and offers some good decision-making along the way.
text_fidelity_b: Ludonaute Fantasy Flight Games LUCV01 Carta Imperia Victoria, Multicolor

The description for child use I feel is risky advertising because of the nature of how a child could squeeze or play with the ball & in what setting. For instance in school a pencil could penetrate the ball causing it to break open & it’s a mess. The individual balls inside could also be a choking hazard. There are many instances where a ball is given to a child when the purpose of using it has distractions of other sorts. I feel the balls are durable for adult use as they’ve lasted for me- again my own experience. Stay away if considering to purchase for a child. A good price for three. The purpose absolutely works for me & I’m glad I purchased them.

Just My Style Name Bracelet Maker by Horizon Group USA The loom is intended to make it easier to make braid or bead bracelets. The 6 spools come pre-wrapped with different types of cording. I didn't particularly care for their pre-wrapped selection, however, the spools can be wrapped with whatever cord or thread you want to use. Then you pop the spools into the dispenser section of the loom and slide the axle into place. We had some trouble getting the axle out again. The spools stay in place just fine without the axle, so we have no plans to use it again. You measure out 8 to 12 inches of cord for each strand to create a braided bracelet. You slip the cord into the foam slots near the spools to hold the cord in place, then braid using your own design or the instruction booklet directions. The booklet describes how to make a 3 strand braid, 6 strand braid, braided bracelet where one strand is first beaded, and a friendship bracelet. Though well-illustrated, the instructions were not always clear.

For beaded bracelets, you remove the green foam insets, choose a beading pattern, and set up the beads on the tray. The tray does make threading the beads easier. You place cords on either side of the beads on the board and use the included needle and thread to string the beads and attach them to the cords in rows. Except for the axle, everything worked fine. It would have been nice if the beads were packaged in sealed in zip bags or the like as they keep spilling. I ended up finding bags to put them in.

text_fidelity_a:
DINOTRUX REPTOOL CONTROL TY RUX We gave this to my 8 year old, because he loves all things dinosaurs, and he also likes Dinotrux(which is a Netflix show). He may be a little older than the average child that would want this toy, though.

When I asked him to tell me what he liked or didn't like about Ty, he responded, "I like everything about him!" His favorite parts are that Ty roars when he's first turned on and he dances. He also loves the "hide and seek" feature with Revvit and the fact that he's given directions for what to do.

From the parent's point of view, this thing is really cute, and I love that my boys enjoy him so much. He's sometimes annoying, though. He talks loud! On multiple occasions, I'd find myself jumping when Ty suddenly spoke in his very loud voice. We try not to add too many "loud" toys to our home, and the ones we do usually don't last long, but personally, I've found this one to be worth it. (Some of you won't!)

Overall, this is a really fun toy for Dinotrux fans! All of my boys have enjoyed it, but especially my 8 year old.

text_fidelity_a:
The Lord of the Rings: The Card Game Revised Core Set | Adventure/Cooperative Game for Adults and Teens | Ages 14+ | 1-4 Players | Average Playtime 30-120 Minutes | Made by Fantasy Flight Games First and foremost, this is a LIVING card game. It is not a COLLECTIBLE card game. Big difference! The latter just means that you can buy new expansions to expand your gameplay / add mechanics / etc. The latter means you have to go and buy packs at the store in order to get newer and better cards. In a collectible card game, a billionaire can go and buy all the packs and have the best deck ever. In this game, everyone who buys the game (and its expansion cards) will be on even footing. I find collectible card games to be somewhat predatory given they're essentially like gambling. Okay, on to the review.

High level message is, not great but not bad either. If you love Lord of the Rings you'll have a better experience. If you're neutral on it, then you're not going to enjoy the complicated grind of learning how to play.

Pros
- Beautiful artwork
- Good use of the LOTR lore in the gameplay and story
- Decent length of games - assume 1 to 1.5 hours
- Pretty good mechanics, once you understand them

Cons
- Phew, this game is complicated. The first sign that it's complicated, is the fact that there are TWO rule books, each of hefty size. This is not the kind of game you whip out on game night with a bunch of casual players. You need other folks who are dedicated to play this game, willing to watch a YouTube video together, or something, and then willing to stumble around for the first hour to get this done.
- So many things to keep track of... there's spinners, dials, tokens... did I mention this game is complicated
text_fidelity_b: The Lord of the Rings: The Card Game Revised Core Set | Adventure/Cooperative Game for Adults and Teens | Ages 14+ | 1-4 Players | Average Playtime 30-120 Minutes | Made by Fantasy Flight Games

text_fidelity_a:
Puzzle Conserver, 200 ml I tested this conserver out on a cheap puzzle just to get a good idea of what it was like.

Make sure you shake the bottle well. I purposely left a spot kind of bubbly just to see if it would dry smooth. It does NOT! (as I'm sure most of us suspected) You need to spend time smoothing it out. Even the spots that I worked at smoothing out dried a little "smeary", but from a distance you can't tell. text_fidelity_a:
My Arcade GameStation Wireless - Plug and Play Game Console - 2 Wireless Controllers - 300 Retro Style Games - Battery or USB Powered - Plugs Into TV I like this game console, but really just think it's something that a few people will enjoy more than most. The design of the console is really good, the look of the main unit is very well done. The wireless controllers are decent enough and feel well made. It's the games though that count. The games are a bit underwhelming. There is a good variety of games, from card games (solitaire, go fish, and a few others of that kind) to puzzle games (sudoku, sliding block puzzle, a pattern block puzzle). There are also many arcade style games. This model of the console does not have any of the old Data East arcade games on it. There is another version that does. The front of the box for that one will have graphics showing the Data East games.

I was sort of expecting the games on this to be the same as what is on most of these sort of consoles (famiclone games), but instead these are a bit more generic than even those. Some of the games are difficult to figure out, it took me about 10-15 minutes or experimenting to figure out how the controllers worked with the sudoku game, and even after I did - the controls were so awkward it made playing the game nearly impossible (and given that this game is timed, I never could achieve a decent time in solving the puzzle). Still, there are many that are worth playing. I think one of the reasons I like game systems like this is the challenge of figuring out what makes the game work.

The main game unit take four double A batteries and the wireless units take triple-A batteries (three each). The console hooks to the TV via a composite video cable (yellow RCA plug) and has one audio input (another RCA plug). I'm using the front inputs on my old VCR which is still connected to my television. I like that the controllers are wireless. You don't really need both, many of the games are for single player. The controllers are marked (P1 & P2), as the P1 controller is the main one and it is used to select the games from the menu.

All-in-all, I am enjoying most of these games, and appreciate the game system for what it is - but I would imagine that many people might not.

This system is made by My Arcade Gaming, and I have one of their handheld Go Gamer Portable games which I purchased last year around Christmas time. I was sort of hoping that this new game console would have the same set of games on it that their handheld model has (which are really good by the way), but that wasn't the case.
text_fidelity_b: My Arcade GameStation Wireless - Plug and Play Game Console - 2 Wireless Controllers - 300 Retro Style Games - Battery or USB Powered - Plugs Into TV

text_fidelity_a:
World Series of Yahtzee Board Games [[VIDEOID:9706f008dc0f922f2a22889963de0e00]] This is a digital, board-based game of Yahtzee. I think it's made to compete with [[ASIN:B0042ET8S0 Uno Attack Game]] and [[ASIN:B001G5431A Bunco]], and it is much more fun than both of those games. Sometimes making a classic into a digital version is a mistake, but the designers did an awesome job with this game.

It's still [[ASIN:B00000IWH6 Yahtzee]]. You still get five dice, and you have to match the classic Yahtzee combinations of Yahtzee (five of a kind), four of a kind, three of a kind, full house, small straight (sequence or run) and large straight. But, everybody plays at once with their own sets of five dice, and the computer in the middle moderates everything, so goes very quickly and it's exciting.

The little buzzer in the middle is pretty sophisticated for a simple computer. It records who buzzes in and in which order you buzzed in, and it plays some fun countdown music. You get five seconds after the first person finishes to finish rolling and to buzz in yourself. Each person can collect up to one card per turn, based on what they rolled, but if you're not lucky, or if someone else gets your combination first, then you don't get any cards per turn. Usually turns take about thirty seconds each, and a full game all the way through will take about ten minutes, so it's very fast paced and fun.

I really liked the original Yahtzee, and I really like this too.

Pros:
+Very fun new version of an already fun classic
+Doesn't waste paper like the old version
+No more waiting around for slow players, like the old version
+You really should start playing this instead of Bunco, since there's a lot more strategy in this game
+You can roll the dice as many times as you want, where in traditional Yahtzee, you could only roll the dice three times per turn

Cons:
-The black dice with the red dots are so much cooler than the rest of the dice, so everyone will be fighting over these
-Made out of cheap plastic cardboard. If you love this game, which you probably will, and if you're not a dainty family, which you probably aren't, then you'll break these pretty quickly and go through about one of these games per year. It's still cheaper than a night at the movies, though, and this game is fun enough to justify getting a new one.
text_fidelity_b: World Series of Yahtzee Board Games

TAMIYA Models Chi Ha Type 97 Tank (Japanese) This tank model is superlative with a lot of details to glue on. ( it has no unnecessary steps that one hates and all the details are easy to glue on and there is no awkward steps that will make one curse while doing it) It take more than the time you expected which for an experienced modeler that is a joy t o add one after another small piece to the model and make it looks very real. After it is done it looks like from a $40 dollar kit than a 16 doller kit.
I have always learned something from other people's comment about how a model is made. Here I am going to recommend using epoxy glue for small parts of plastic details. The epoxy glue gives you more time than CA glue for small detail pieces. And the epoxy glue also have thicker substance than CA glue for small pieces so it will stay in place when the small pieces are glued on. The epoxy glue also becomes thicker as time goes on so you can adjust your timing to chose the right time to glue the pieces on to the model. The smaller the pieces the faster you need to glue on the model and the larger piece you can wait until is becomes very thick before using it. Another trick about dealing with those shining drops left unintentionally on the models; I usually drop some power ( you can use fine grain white pepper dust) onto the drop of glue before it is dried. This will eliminate those ugly sheen of glue and later the glued dust can be painted as rust for weathering.
All in all this little model (about 6 inches long) is well worth your money. It looks far better than other 16 dollar model kits and i can guarantee it.
text_fidelity_b: TAMIYA Models Chi Ha Type 97 Tank (Japanese)

text_fidelity_a: Air Hogs - Supernova, Gravity Defying Hand-Controlled Flying Orb, for Ages 8 and Up Still learning!!  This has had our house in a happy uproar since we got it!  After multiple readings of directions and many try outs we think we kind of have a handle on the basics but doing any tricks are an accidental result only.  Batteries are already in this.  Everything for power is concentrated in the center of this orb.  It comes w/USB to charge through our computer.  There is a tiny, tiny white slide tab in center by batteries that you move to turn this on.  Immediately (if charged) the center ball light will come on and flash colors.  When charging or a problem, the ball light will flash red only.  This is a fairly fragile  plastic caged flyer.  It doesn't weigh a lot because it has to keep it's self flying + hovering with 4 little sets of plastic blades that rotate (think fan blades).  Four extra blades come with this. Inside the orb besides the power center and the blades are sensors that will cause the orb to change directions when they are blocked in any way. To start, you have it on and slowly let it drop out of yr hands, it will drop and start hovering before it actually hits the floor(the sensors realize there is something in the way). After it starts hovering low over floor you get a hand(s) underneath and just start raising it and moving it all over the place by using yr hands to block the sensors...All the while, center light is flashing colors and the orb is making this noise..lol, between a whine & buzz and you find yrself almost running around the room trying to control this thing!  It will go up to the ceiling and then you have to figure out how to get a hand up to control it!  We don't dare take it outside to do, afraid it wouldn't come back!  This has fallen to the floor several times and not broken but, it is something you should take care with.  A lot of great accidental exercise and laughs!  Not for little children to use but they will love the show
text_fidelity_b: Air Hogs - Supernova, Gravity Defying Hand-Controlled Flying Orb, for Ages 8 and Up

Zynga Draw Something Game For years now app makers have been taking your favorite childhood games and turning them into apps. Welp, Hasbro has had enough of that and has decided to turn the tables on them. Now your favorite adulthood apps have been turned into good old fashioned board games. Take that app designers!

No, really. The Draw Something app that is so popular amongst your co-workers, it is now a board game. Packaged in a giant pencil box (odd as the writing utensils it arrives with are crayons) you get enough of what you need for up to four people to play (coin tracker clips, crayons, draw stations, and paper pads) in addition to that you get 180 word cards and a game guide.

Appropriate for the whole family (unless you have some of THOSE types of adults -- you know the ones). Great for people who want to practice their drawing skills, encourage the kiddies to be creative, or just get the family away from the electronics (what better way to trick them into a family fun night than by using a board game of their favorite app?).

The official site doesn't list replacement parts for sale which is no big deal for crayons but could be for the game pads so if you're a prolific arteest you'll have to find the right sized paper pads or make your own.

Matchbox Cars Playset, 4-Level Toy Garage & Tow Truck in 1:64 Scale, Kid-Powered Elevator, Car Repair Station & Spiral Ramp For my 4 and a half year old grandson. He loves his cars and so this was a nice compact "repair garage" play structure. It will not be something you will want to break down daily and store, it will need to be up and available for immediate play. It will stay at my house for his visits and be stored on a closet shelf between visits. It came with one little tow truck vehicle. There is no car storage; this is just a play activity. A turning knob on top of the elevator brings cars up to individual floor levels and there are gates on the ramps that divert the cars to a car maintenance floor and a car wash floor in the structure. Although it says it's 4 level, there is nothing but a ramp from the elevator on the upper level and the lower level is really just the entry to the elevator and an open accessible area underneath that the imagination can invent a use for.

The instructions were also less than stellar and being only in black and white, identifying some of the little pieces was sometimes guesswork. There are small pieces that can be pulled off, so observe the recommended age group for this toy. We were not interested in all the many decorative stickers that can be applied on this toy, so only used what we wanted to.

It appears to be sturdy enough and, if incorporated with some other play structures, could keep his attention for a lengthy period of play time.

Dominion 2nd Edition | Deckbuilding Strategy Game for 2-4 Players, Ages 13+ | Updated Cards, Artwork, Streamlined Rules This is the best deck building game EVER!!
I am in my 20's and have only recently been introduced to deck building games, and instantly fell in love.
DOminion and the DC Comic deck games are my favorite, but Dominion provides a larger variety because the cards used change.
The game its self comes with several possible versions of the game.
For example, the game is plaid with several action card decks to draw from, but Dominion comes with twice as many action cards. So, no game is exactly alike. The rule book comes with various options of which action cards to play with for certain kinds of games.
This game is dynamic!

I first played Dominion at a bar with board games. After a few times I fell in love and bought this second edition. The cards are beautiful, more colorful than the first edition. (I attached some photos to see to see the cards)

It says that the game can be played in about 30 minutes... for me it takes closer to an hour with 3 players. It also probably depends on what type of game you play (which actions cards to choose to play with) But because we are still learning, maybe we go a little slower, constantly re reading what the action cards say/do.

At the end of the game, who ever has the most victory points wins.
text_fidelity_b: Dominion 2nd Edition | Deckbuilding Strategy Game for 2-4 Players, Ages 13+ | Updated Cards, Artwork, Streamlined Rules

Thames & Kosmos Word Slam Family | Fast-Paced Multiplayer Party Card & Word Game | High Playercount | Based On The Award Winning Word Slam Word Slam Family is a nice game that's easy to play, despite the dense rule sheet that comes with the game. You can set this up and play it quickly, and it's easy enough that it truly is a family weight game. You don't even need to be a reader to get some of the clues, assuming an adult is there to help.

It's a one-word for one-word style association game, that, quite frankly, is done better by most of it's competitors. I think that this one might appeal to those who really like the small box size, or who haven't played any competitors, but as someone who has, this adds nothing new to the genre, and does not have the staying power of it's rivals.

text_fidelity_a:
Thames & Kosmos Lost Cities: Rivals Card Game | Strategy Auction Adventure | Vibrant Colors for Two to Four Players | Family Friendly Fun by Kosmos This is the third major rendition of the "Lost Cities" games (the card game, the board game, and now Rivals). Each is a game that is ostensibly about discovering lost cities, but is really about putting numbered cards in order. None are special games in my collection, although I now own all three, and all are well-loved by some gamers in the world. Rivals is potentially the most interesting of them, as it introduces a new auction mechanic into the standard put-numbers-in-order formula, but while I found this auction to be a new and interesting method of getting cards, the two other people who I've played it with are not convinced that it's fun so much as it's mean.

I think if you don't mind a game where you play one on one and directly attack others, then this might be something you can handle. I believe that while the others are light-hearted and super easy for anyone to pick up, this suffers from the "meanness" problem, and also from the fact that the more experienced player will easily dispatch newcomers. As many who love Lost CIities have a partner in mind for when they play, and tend not to play with outsiders, this may not be a problem for Rivals, but this is certainly more intense of a "game" than those, and is not always the light hearted fare that the old classics tend to be.

If you want a light, non-interactive card game, then the other Lost Cities are better choices. If you need something more interesting, then this is a good chocie.
text_fidelity_b: Thames & Kosmos Lost Cities: Rivals Card Game | Strategy Auction Adventure | Vibrant Colors for Two to Four Players | Family Friendly Fun by Kosmos

LEGO Ideas Tree House 21318, Model Construction Set for 16 Plus Year Olds with 3 Cabins, Interchangeable Leaves, Minifigures and a Bird Figure This is an impressive LEGO set. First of all, the box is FULL of bricks., I dislike toys (or breakfast cereals!) that come in half-empty boxes. This is filled to the brim.

The treehouse set is not an easy set to build. Some parts of it are tricky, requiring gentle, patient hands.
Also, I have noticed in a few recent sets of things that I do not like. As I was building the bridge from one room to another, an essential piece was missing. It is LEGO, you can work around that sort of problem. In the last bag of the set, there was the missing piece. It was not needed on any of the steps for the last bag, it seems like it was "hidden" to frustrate me.

That said, when done it is simply beautiful. I built it with the fall leaves, and in spring, I will remove those and add the green leaves back!

Part of what makes this an advanced set is the physics of it. The small LEGO trunk should not be able to sustain the weight of the branches. However, some clever building techniques reinforce the trunk so it can easily carry the weight.

A spectacular build. Well worth the frustrations. A set to be enjoyed for many years to come!
text_fidelity_b: LEGO Ideas Tree House 21318, Model Construction Set for 16 Plus Year Olds with 3 Cabins, Interchangeable Leaves, Minifigures and a Bird Figure

Still the price was reasonable so I ordered one. This is not the first Klutz craft kit we've played with - so it was a familiar experience as those other kits. There really wasn't much in the box - the clay, a pencil (without an eraser), a sculpting tool, and a couple sheets of foldable paper props for the erasers you make (if you make the ones shown in the instructional guide).

You get plenty of different color clay - if you limit yourself to making fairly small erasers. The clay we got wasn't dried out - but it did take some kneeding to get soft enough to shape. Baking the erasers was simple - we used a toaster oven. Just be sure to use the right temperature and watch the erasers while they bake to make sure none start melting. Baking time can vary - mostly 15 to 30 minutes depending on the size & shape of the erasers you made.

The erasers are more ornamental than practical - but they do erase most pencil marks.

We're having fun with this kit - the instructional guide is outstanding. I'm happy with my purchase.
